Retirement Planning

Make Your Savings Last

Saving for retirement is only half the plan. The other half is turning what you’ve built into income that lasts as long as you need it, without taking on more risk than you’re comfortable with.

Take the Retirement Readiness Assessment Find a Local Professional

Why It Matters

Key Areas to Consider

Retirement can last 20 or 30 years, sometimes longer. A thoughtful plan for how and when you use your savings can help your money keep pace with rising costs, market ups and downs, and the expenses that are hard to predict.

Planning for a Longer Life

People are living longer than ever. Planning for a longer retirement can help reduce the risk of outliving your savings, especially for couples, where one spouse may live well into their 90s.

Your Withdrawal Strategy

How much you take out each year, and which accounts you draw from first, can affect both how long your money lasts and how much of it goes to taxes.

Market Ups and Downs

A market decline early in retirement can have a bigger impact than one later on. Balancing growth with stability can help protect the income you rely on.

Rising Prices

Even modest inflation reduces what your money can buy over time. A strong plan accounts for higher costs on groceries, utilities, and other everyday essentials.

Questions to Ask Yourself

Is Your Plan Ready?

  • Do I know how much I can comfortably withdraw each year?
  • Which accounts should I draw from first?
  • How would a market downturn affect my plans?
  • Have I planned for a retirement that could last 30 years or more?
  • Is my spouse protected if something happens to me?
  • Do I have a plan for large, unexpected expenses?

Not sure how to answer? The Retirement Readiness Assessment can help you see where you stand.

Strategies to Explore

How a Retirement Professional Can Help

  1. 1

    Build a Retirement Budget

    Separate essential expenses, like housing, food, and healthcare, from the things you’d like to do, like travel and hobbies. Knowing the difference makes every other decision easier.

  2. 2

    Cover the Essentials First

    Many retirees aim to cover essential expenses with dependable income sources such as Social Security, pensions, or annuities, so day-to-day needs aren’t tied to the market.

  3. 3

    Coordinate Your Withdrawals

    The order in which you use taxable, tax-deferred, and tax-free accounts can help your savings last longer and may reduce the taxes you pay over time.

  4. 4

    Review Your Plan Regularly

    Markets, tax laws, and your own needs change. Revisiting your plan each year, and after major life events, helps keep it on track.

Healthcare & Long-Term Care

Prepare for Healthcare Costs

Healthcare is one of the most significant, and least predictable, expenses in retirement. Planning ahead for medical bills, prescriptions, and potential long-term care can help protect both your savings and your independence.

Take the Retirement Readiness Assessment Find a Local Professional

Why It Matters

Key Areas to Consider

Medicare helps with many healthcare costs, but it doesn’t cover everything. Premiums, deductibles, copays, prescriptions, and extended care services can add up quickly when they haven’t been part of the plan.

Gaps in Medicare

Original Medicare leaves some costs to you. Medicare Supplement and Medicare Advantage plans offer different ways to help fill those gaps, each with its own trade-offs.

Prescription Drugs

Drug costs can vary widely from one plan to the next. Reviewing your coverage each year helps make sure the medications you rely on are still covered.

Long-Term Care

Help with daily activities, whether at home, in assisted living, or in a nursing facility, is generally not covered by Medicare for extended stays and can quickly draw down savings.

Short-Term Recovery

A fall, surgery, or illness can mean weeks of care. Short-term and extended care coverage is designed to help with those costs without a long-term commitment.

Questions to Ask Yourself

Is Your Plan Ready?

  • Do I understand what my Medicare coverage does and doesn’t pay for?
  • Are my prescriptions covered under my current plan?
  • How would I pay for care if I needed help with daily activities?
  • Would a long-term care event affect my spouse’s financial security?
  • Have I talked with my family about my care preferences?
  • When did I last review my healthcare coverage?

Not sure how to answer? The Retirement Readiness Assessment can help you see where you stand.

Strategies to Explore

How a Retirement Professional Can Help

  1. 1

    Review Your Medicare Options

    Comparing plans during enrollment periods can help you find coverage that fits your doctors, prescriptions, and budget, and avoid costly surprises.

  2. 2

    Plan for Extended Care

    Long-term care, extended care, and hybrid policies are designed to help pay for care when you need it, so your retirement savings can stay focused on income.

  3. 3

    Set Aside Funds for Out-of-Pocket Costs

    Building healthcare into your retirement budget, including premiums and copays, helps keep unexpected bills from disrupting your plans.

  4. 4

    Make Your Wishes Known

    Talking with loved ones and putting your preferences in writing can reduce stress for your family if they ever need to make decisions on your behalf.

Home / Retirement Income

Retirement Income

Plan for Reliable Income

A dependable paycheck doesn’t stop mattering when you retire. Creating a steady income stream can give you the confidence to enjoy retirement without worrying about how the bills will get paid.

Take the Retirement Readiness Assessment Find a Local Professional

Why It Matters

Key Areas to Consider

Most retirees rely on a mix of income sources. Coordinating them, so the right money arrives at the right time, can make a meaningful difference in your monthly budget and your peace of mind.

Social Security Timing

When you claim benefits can affect how much you receive for the rest of your life. The right time depends on your health, other income, and your spouse’s benefits.

Pensions & Employer Plans

Pension payout elections and 401(k) rollover decisions are often permanent, so it helps to understand every option before you choose.

Income That Lasts

Some annuities can provide income for life, helping cover essential expenses regardless of how the markets perform, subject to the claims-paying ability of the issuing insurer.

Taxes on Your Income

Different income sources are taxed in different ways. Coordinating them may help you keep more of what you’ve earned over the course of retirement.

Questions to Ask Yourself

Is Your Plan Ready?

  • Will my dependable income sources cover my essential expenses?
  • Do I know the best time to claim Social Security?
  • What happens to my household income if my spouse passes away?
  • Am I prepared for income needs that change over time?
  • Do I have a plan for required minimum distributions?
  • How will inflation affect my income in 10 or 20 years?

Not sure how to answer? The Retirement Readiness Assessment can help you see where you stand.

Strategies to Explore

How a Retirement Professional Can Help

  1. 1

    Map Out Your Income Sources

    List every source of retirement income, how much it pays, and when it begins. Seeing it all in one place often reveals gaps, or opportunities.

  2. 2

    Match Income to Expenses

    Pairing dependable income with essential expenses, and more flexible sources with discretionary spending, can help bring stability to your budget.

  3. 3

    Explore Lifetime Income Options

    Annuities and other income strategies can be designed to provide payments for life. A professional can help you weigh the benefits, costs, and trade-offs.

  4. 4

    Plan for Taxes & Distributions

    Thoughtful timing of withdrawals and required minimum distributions may help manage your tax bill and keep more income working for you.

About Retirement Professional

Retirement Professional helps people approaching or living in retirement understand their options and connect with licensed professionals in their community.

What We Do

Retirement can bring big decisions: how to make savings last, how to prepare for healthcare and long-term care costs, and how to create income you can count on. Our goal is to make those topics easier to understand and to make it simple to find someone local who can help.

  • Education. Plain-language articles on retirement income, healthcare costs, and protecting your savings.
  • Guidance. The complimentary Retirement Readiness Assessment helps you see where you stand and what to explore next.
  • Local support. Our Find a Professional tool connects you with licensed insurance agents who serve your area.

Who You’ll Work With

The professionals featured on RetirementProfessional.com are independently licensed insurance agents affiliated with GoldenCare, an Integrity company. Each agent is responsible for the products and advice they provide, and products are offered through the agent and the insurance companies they represent.

What We Are Not

Retirement Professional is not an insurance company, does not issue policies, and is not affiliated with Medicare or any government agency. The information on this site is educational and is not tax, legal, or investment advice.

Questions? Contact us at privacy@retirementprofessional.com.

Privacy Notice

Last updated: November 23, 2026

This Privacy Notice explains how RetirementProfessional.com (“Retirement Professional,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, and shares personal information when you visit our website, take the Retirement Readiness Assessment, or ask to be connected with a licensed professional.

1. Information We Collect

Information you give us. When you complete a form or the Retirement Readiness Assessment, we may collect your name, email address, phone number, ZIP code, and your answers to assessment questions. Some answers may relate to your retirement savings, income sources, household, and healthcare or long-term care planning.

Information collected automatically. Like most websites, we and our service providers may automatically collect your IP address, browser and device type, pages viewed, referring website, and the advertising campaign or link that brought you to the site (for example, UTM parameters or click identifiers).

Cookies and similar technologies. We may use cookies, pixels, and similar tools to operate the site, remember preferences, measure performance, and support advertising. Embedded content, such as YouTube videos and Google Fonts, may also collect information under those providers’ own privacy policies. Videos on our site load only after you choose to play them.

2. How We Use Information

  • To provide your assessment results and educational resources you request
  • To connect you with a licensed insurance professional who serves your area
  • To respond to your questions and requests
  • To operate, secure, and improve our website
  • To measure and improve our marketing
  • To comply with legal obligations and protect our rights

3. How We Share Information

With licensed professionals. When you request a consultation, submit a form on an agent’s page, or take the assessment from an agent’s link, we share your contact information and responses with that licensed insurance agent and their agency, GoldenCare, an Integrity company, so they can contact you. Their use of your information is governed by their own privacy notices, including the Integrity Privacy Notice.

With service providers. We use vendors for website hosting, form processing, customer relationship management, communications, and analytics. They may use your information only to provide services to us.

For legal reasons. We may disclose information to comply with law, respond to lawful requests, or protect the rights and safety of our users and others.

Business transfers. If our business is sold or reorganized, information may transfer as part of that transaction.

We do not sell your personal information for money. Some advertising and analytics activities may be considered “sharing” or “targeted advertising” under certain state laws; see our Do Not Sell or Share page to opt out.

4. Your Choices and Rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information; to obtain a copy of it; and to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information, targeted advertising, and certain profiling. You may also withdraw consent to receive calls or text messages at any time.

To make a request, email privacy@retirementprofessional.com. We will verify your request and respond within the time required by law. You may use an authorized agent to make a request on your behalf, and we will not discriminate against you for exercising your rights. If we deny your request, you may appeal by replying to our decision.

5. Consumer Health Data

Some assessment questions may relate to your health or healthcare planning. Our Consumer Health Data Privacy Notice explains how we handle that information.

6. Data Security and Retention

We use reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect personal information. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure. We keep personal information only as long as needed for the purposes described in this notice or as required by law.

7. Children

Our website is intended for adults and is not directed to children under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

8. Changes to This Notice

We may update this notice from time to time. The “Last updated” date above shows when it was last revised.

9. Contact Us

Email privacy@retirementprofessional.com with any questions about this notice or our privacy practices.

Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information

Last updated: November 23, 2026

You have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information and the use of your information for targeted advertising.

How We Use Advertising Technology

We do not sell personal information for money. We may use cookies and similar technologies from advertising and analytics partners to measure our campaigns and show relevant ads. Under some state privacy laws, this may be considered “selling,” “sharing,” or “targeted advertising.”

How to Opt Out

  • Email us at privacy@retirementprofessional.com with the subject line “Do Not Sell or Share.” Include the name, email address, and phone number you used with us so we can locate your information.
  • Use a browser signal. We treat a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal from your browser as a valid opt-out request for that browser.
  • Adjust your browser settings to block or delete cookies. Some features may not work as intended.

Information Shared With Agents

When you ask to be connected with a licensed professional, your information is shared with that agent and their agency so they can respond to your request. To opt out of the agency’s practices, use the Integrity “Do Not Sell or Share” request form.

We will not discriminate against you for exercising your privacy rights. See our Privacy Notice for more information.

Home / Consumer Health Data

Consumer Health Data Privacy Notice

Last updated: November 23, 2026

This notice supplements our Privacy Notice and applies to “consumer health data” as defined by laws such as Washington’s My Health My Data Act and Nevada’s consumer health data law.

Consumer Health Data We Collect

When you take the Retirement Readiness Assessment or contact a professional, you may share information that relates to your health, such as whether health issues have caused financial stress, your healthcare and long-term care planning, or coverage you are considering. We may also infer general planning needs from your answers.

How We Collect It

We collect consumer health data directly from you when you answer assessment questions or submit a form, and only with your consent.

Why We Use It

  • To provide your personalized assessment results
  • To connect you with a licensed professional who can discuss options with you, at your request
  • To respond to your questions and operate the services you request

We do not use consumer health data for targeted advertising, and we do not sell it.

Who We Share It With

With your consent, we share consumer health data with the licensed insurance agent you are connected with and their agency, GoldenCare, an Integrity company, and with service providers who process it on our behalf under contract.

Your Rights

You may have the right to confirm whether we collect, share, or sell your consumer health data; to access it, including a list of third parties and affiliates it was shared with; to withdraw consent; and to request deletion. To exercise these rights, email privacy@retirementprofessional.com. If we deny your request, you may appeal by replying to our decision, and if your appeal is denied you may contact your state Attorney General.

Home / SMS/MMS Terms

SMS/MMS Terms

Last updated: November 23, 2026

These terms apply when you agree to receive text messages related to Retirement Professional or a licensed professional you connect with through RetirementProfessional.com.

Consent

By providing your mobile number and agreeing to receive texts, you consent to receive recurring automated and conversational messages, such as appointment reminders, follow-up on your requests, and educational updates, from Retirement Professional and the licensed agent you are connected with. Consent is not a condition of any purchase.

Message Frequency and Cost

Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Check with your wireless carrier for details about your plan.

How to Stop or Get Help

Reply STOP to any message to opt out. You will receive one message confirming your opt-out, and no further texts will be sent unless you opt in again. Reply HELP for help, or email privacy@retirementprofessional.com.

Carriers and Privacy

Wireless carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. We do not sell or share mobile numbers or text messaging opt-in consent with third parties for their own marketing. See our Privacy Notice for details on how we handle your information.
